study.question: Does the stronger joint model require the auxiliary-odd orientation bit s(Q), or can a click-only, auxiliary-even pivot bit retain its validation benefit at matched nuisance line, radius and support?
study.hypothesis: The retained nuisance-line bit carries useful auxiliary-dependent orientation beyond a generic varying sign. Replacing s(Q) by the first-max-absolute pivot sign s(K) of the centered click-only context cotangent will reduce the negative-arm click AUC and weaken the external-sign contrast. This is a conditional local hypothesis, not established by existing canonicalization comparisons. A competitive click-bit replacement would undermine the necessity of this auxiliary-odd bit, while leaving auxiliary magnitude/line/gate utility open.

inherited_components: Entire joint model: field embeddings, frozen masked inputs, compressed uniform/feedback histories, DIN scorer, temporal/match details, task residual adapters, rank16 context-history product modules and four towers.
Joint-context custom autograd collector and FP64 aggregate/centering/projection machinery; original half-batch tangent Q and K/H nuisance construction.

From g3-r0056 nuisance canonicalization and auxiliary-bit replay implementations; g3-r0055 negative incumbent is empirical parent.
study.proposed_difference: Add a state-free training-only helper: center click_gradient over occupied rows in FP64 to obtain K; choose its first flattened maximal-absolute pivot, set s(K)=-1 for a negative pivot and +1 otherwise (including K=0); multiply the inherited canonical nuisance line V by s(K). No extra validity gate. Candidate transfer is +/-s(K)V; bridges remain +/-s(Q)V. All cells compute V, both bit sources and both signs before selection. Only one shared-context VJP selection changes; scalar joint BCE remains unchanged and the surrogate is explicitly not its derivative.
predictions: At identical reducer inputs, all four arms have the same zero support, Frobenius transfer norm and unoriented nuisance line up to numerical precision; candidate/bridge differences are global signs only.

Holding click/state fixed and reversing all auxiliary context cotangents should reverse the auxiliary-bit transfer and preserve the click-bit transfer away from finite-precision gates/ties; zero cases remain defined.

Predeclared performance direction: AUC(aux_bit_negative_bridge) > AUC(click_bit_negative). The auxiliary negative-minus-positive contrast is predicted larger than the click-bit negative-minus-positive contrast.

The new modules and bridges should have identical initial outputs, scalar loss, private gradients and running-state updates at fixed state; bridge click AUC should replay 0.6689064289769298 and 0.6679524177535937 under deterministic host execution.
No inference architecture or parameter change is expected. Training adds a small FP64 centering/pivot helper equally to all cells; actual cost must be measured.
falsifiers: If either click-bit sign matches or exceeds the auxiliary negative bridge, necessity of the auxiliary-odd bit is not supported in this seed; report both arms and the interaction rather than selecting a favorable sign post hoc.
If the predicted bit-source by external-sign interaction is zero or reversed, the specific signed-orientation explanation loses support even if one candidate improves.

Forward/private-gradient/state mismatch at fixed state, unequal support/norm/line, or failed auxiliary-reversal parity invalidates the intended bit-only interpretation; no mechanism conclusion from those runs.
If s(K) and s(Q) almost always agree or disagree, the replacement fails to separate information sources; report measured agreement and call attribution unresolved.
Failure of exact replay requires execution/numerical diagnosis before interpreting historical AUC differences. Single-seed improvements remain preliminary.
alternative_explanations: Single fixed seed and adaptively selected validation history; exact replay is not independent seed support.
Click-bit and auxiliary-bit frequencies, temporal persistence, pivot ties and association with training state are not matched.
The auxiliary norm, absolute overlap used to build the nuisance exclusion and original validity support remain in both arms; this does not remove all auxiliary information.
FP64 row-space geometry precedes one cast, repeated-ID sparse scatter, dense clipping and adaptive optimization; orthogonality is not guaranteed in parameter/update space.
Trajectories diverge after the first different update; geometry is only matched on identical states, not across later learned states.
The original bit may merely choose a favorable mean sign or switching pattern; the replacement may change marginal sign counts rather than informative alignment.
The arbitrary maximum-coordinate pivot depends on batch/feature ordering; this suite does not establish a coordinate-invariant semantic direction.
Auxiliary labels are broad user/category/brand24h signals and official offline historical actions may not be mature online; no production causality claim.
